tracks.narration: What if the feedback path of an op-amp were a capacitor instead of a resistor? You'd build a time integrator.
Same inverting topology: V plus grounded, input through R into V minus, feedback from V out back to V minus — but the feedback element is a capacitor C, not a resistor.
Virtual short forces V minus to ground. So the current through R is V in over R, and that same current charges the capacitor — meaning dV out over dt equals minus V in over R C.
Feed in a square wave. During each half cycle V in is constant, so V out ramps down at minus V in over R C — out comes a triangle wave whose slope is set entirely by R times C.
An op-amp integrator turns a square wave into a triangle wave, and more generally turns any input into its running time integral — with R times C setting the slope.
